shared_elements: low relief carving on a rough, unpolished stone surface
horizontal register/row of repeated rectangular box-like units along the upper edge
small disc or oval element within the field
stone photographed in situ with surrounding earth/rubble
justification: The most specific correspondence is the shared compositional scheme of an upper band of repeated rectangular cells, each containing a rounded or U-shaped inner form, set off by a horizontal divider above a larger field with an enclosed oval/loop motif, all executed in shallow, softly rounded relief on unfinished stone. The biggest difference is content and handling below that band: B carries clearly recognisable profile animals (quadrupeds and a long-necked bird) rendered in modelled, curvilinear relief, whereas A's lower field is purely angular and geometric with rectilinear meanders and no identifiable creature, and A is a low irregular boulder rather than an upright shaped pillar.
